headline_marked: [[Over 200 migrants rescued]] off Greek coast; most are from Bangladesh and Sudan
headline: Over 200 migrants rescued off Greek coast; most are from Bangladesh and Sudan
summary: More than 200 irregular migrants, predominantly from Bangladesh and Sudan, were rescued by Greek authorities after crossing the Mediterranean Sea by boat, arriving at the island of Crete.
details: Greek authorities rescued over 200 irregular migrants attempting to cross the Mediterranean Sea by boat to the coast of Greece. The majority of those rescued are citizens of Bangladesh and Sudan, with some Egyptians also among the group.

The arrivals of irregular migrants by boat to the southern Greek island of Crete continue, with local newspaper Demokratia reporting that at least 202 migrants reached Crete in successive boat journeys from Libya in less than 48 hours.
This influx of migrants has further increased pressure on the island's local authorities and existing migrant reception centers.
On Thursday morning, a new boat carrying 40 migrants arrived in Ierapetra, southeastern Crete, after being identified by a Frontex aircraft, Europe's border and coast guard agency.
A patrol vessel from the coast guard, aided by a fishing boat, brought the migrants to Ierapetra port, where they were registered and their identities began to be verified.

Hours earlier, 112 migrants had arrived in two other boats. The first boat carried 56 people, comprising 31 Sudanese and 25 Bangladeshi nationals. The second boat also had 56 migrants, with 47 from Bangladesh and nine from Egypt.
All rescued migrants are currently housed in a temporary shelter at Heraklion port. This facility is accommodating new arrivals as the number of migrants on Crete continues to rise.

headline: Death toll rises on Sherpur-Telibazar highway; 9 killed in recent bus collision
summary: Nine people were killed in a bus collision on the Sherpur-Telibazar section of the Sylhet-Dhaka highway on Friday. This accident adds to a concerning trend, with 117 fatalities in 185 accidents across Sylhet district in the last six months.
details: Nine lives were lost instantly in a bus collision on the Sherpur-Telibazar section of the Sylhet-Dhaka highway on Friday. All victims were passengers of the Unique bus, including Saiful Islam who was visiting Sylhet with friends and could not return home.

This tragic incident is part of a worrying trend in Sylhet district, where 117 people have died in 185 accidents over the past six months. Passengers are increasingly concerned about their safety on these routes.

The approximately 35-kilometer stretch from Sherpur to Telibazar on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway is particularly accident-prone, with frequent incidents. In May, seven laborers died when a truck hit their pickup van on this same section.

Drivers attribute many accidents to the poor condition of the roads and the illegal movement of unauthorized vehicles on the highway. They emphasize that these factors significantly contribute to the high number of crashes.

Shofiqur Rahman Chowdhury, convener of the 'Nirapod Sarak Chai' (Safe Road Want) Sylhet district committee, points to unskilled drivers and reckless speeding as major causes. He highlights that multiple factors combine to create dangerous driving conditions.

According to Sherpur Highway Police Officer-in-Charge Anisur Rahman, driver fatigue during long journeys is a significant factor in this region's accident proneness. He notes that exhaustion can impair judgment and reaction times.

Rahman expressed optimism that the completion of the ongoing 6-lane highway project will significantly reduce accidents in the area. Improved infrastructure is expected to enhance safety and traffic flow.
